title: Mono Basin roads: ordered, connected centrelines from OpenStreetMap by way ID, with ODbL attribution
phase: Phase 5 - Mono Basin corridor (moved ahead by ADR 0006)
forbidden_dependencies: Geometry from Google Maps or Street View
acceptance_criteria: FETCH: fetch_osm_roads.py asks Overpass for the way IDs in data/reference/roads.geojson plus the named roads in the world box, records the query, the response timestamp and the OSM data timestamp in the manifest, and caches the raw response under data/raw/ (gitignored). Way IDs that OSM no longer has are listed, not hidden.
CHECK TAGS: for every road, the OSM highway, ref, name and surface tags are compared with the surface, ref and speed in roads.geojson; every disagreement is reported in the manifest.

ORDER: road_graph.py joins ways into ordered, connected centrelines per named road (shared end nodes, correct direction, split at junctions). Every output line has no gap over 200 m between consecutive points; end-to-end distance is within 5 % of line length for roads that do not loop.
TESTS: python -m unittest tests pass using small synthetic way sets (reversed ways, shuffled order, a T junction, a gap, a loop).

ATTRIBUTION: docs/ATTRIBUTION.md carries the OpenStreetMap and USGS credit lines and the ODbL note from R-0002 section 8, reviewed against the licence text; the share-alike question for the shipped game is flagged for the director.
REAL RUN: SR 120 from US-395 to the Yosemite entrance reads as one line of about 13 to 20 km ending near Tioga Pass; US-395 spans the box north to south; SR 270 reaches Bodie.
